advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test resolving `overlap_verdict_batch` via `response_model_for` that validates a batched response with a mixed-case/out-of-enum `relation` and asserts _norm_relation coerces it (and that the entry carries all four base overlap_verdict fields).
evidence: docstring claim contracts.py:206-208 'the relation enum, its normalizing validator ... must never be able to drift apart' — a behavioral contract with no test
ABSENCE: `search_files _norm_relation` in tests/ returns no matches; `search_files overlap_verdict_batch` in tests/ returns no matches

judge.py:190-197 `_verdict()` passes `payload.get('relation', ...)` through WITHOUT normalization; aggregate() (judge.py:237,244) compares relation by exact string, so an un-normalized relation silently fails to surface
test runners (_SeqRunner, _CannedBatchRunner, _RecordingRunner, _PipelineRunner) all return raw dicts, so the model validator never executes in any test
advisory.finding: The new overlap_verdict_batch contract model (OverlapVerdictEntry and its inherited _norm_relation validator) has no test. Every judge/judge_batch test uses a fake runner that returns raw dicts, bypassing the pydantic model; judge.py's _verdict() does not re-normalize relation, and aggregate() matches relation strings exactly ('duplicates', _DIRECTIONAL). So the model's relation-normalizing validator is the sole guard that a raw out-of-enum or mixed-case relation from the batched response is coerced to 'related_distinct', yet no test resolves overlap_verdict_batch via response_model_for or asserts the batched entry normalizes relation / preserves the four base fields the docstring claims are single-sourced.
scenarios: The model echoes a relation as 'Duplicates' or ' depends_on ' (case/whitespace) in a batched entry — validator must fold it, but nothing verifies this path
A future refactor decouples the batched entry from OverlapVerdict, dropping the shared validator; no test catches the drift the docstring forbids
